articles.title: 25 Years Since Its Reveal, and People Still Search for iPods “Every Two Seconds” on eBay
articles.summary: It’s October 23, 2001. Headline: “Apple Presents iPod”. It promised "1,000 songs in your pocket" and fundamentally sparked what turned Apple into the most valuable electronics brand in the world. Yet, a quarter of a century later, Apple’s official storefronts bear no trace of it.
body: iPod is still going strong in the secondhand market, however, at least according to the latest marketplace data from eBay. Nostalgia for the iconic device is clear, with someone searching for an "iPod" on eBay "every two seconds worldwide".
This renaissance aligns with a broader consumer revolution according to eBay, with 76% of consumers surveyed having shopped secondhand in the past year.

Or, perhaps, this could also represent more evidence for an even greater shift in the tech industry. Stop me if you’ve heard this one before, but everything is rather expensive right now, isn’t it? Groundbreaking, I know. So let’s narrow the scope a little further.

Streaming is front and center for a lot of consumers right now. Whether that’s Netflix and Disney+ for film and TV, or Spotify for music streaming. And there’s a monthly cost attached to instantly stream media; we all know this. But it’s a cost that continues to tick upward, without offering any greater value to the consumer.

articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Episodes 7-9 Recap and Review
articles.summary: Avatar: Seven Havens Episodes 7-9 recap and review: Lore and laughter dominate the latest episodes of the series.
body: Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Avatar: Seven Havens Season 1, Episodes 7-9!

Whoa, doggy (and we can say that because non-hybrid dogs exist in the world of Avatar)1 After last week’s episodes of Seven Havens seemed to settle into a nice, comfortable rhythm, this week’s trio literally and figuratively tossed the table with some huge story moves and big additions to the mythology while somehow also managing to be the most effortlessly funny episodes thus far. At least a portion of that is due to the show’s first two-part episode, which you know has to be big — and it is — but thanks to the continued impressive balance of ongoing mysteries and emotional storytelling, Episodes 7-9 are a thrilling roller-coaster ride from start to finish.
Oh, and also we get to see Korra and Asami again, so commence freaking out, everyone!
points: Avatar: Seven Havens Episodes 7-9 recap and review: Lore and laughter dominate the latest episodes of the series.

articles.summary: Yet that’s exactly what Chancellor Kayoko (Jennifer Sun Bell) does at the end of episode 6 when she sends out an emergency radio transmission: “This is Ellora calling any and all Havens,” she says. “We need you.”
body: Despite the name, Avatar: Seven Havens has focused almost exclusively on Ellora, the Haven of Wind and Sand situated somewhere in the desert expanses of the post-apocalyptic world. The first six episodes established that the remote Havens are, for the most part, disconnected from one another. In Ellora, it’s even illegal to contact another Haven without permission from the council.
Her plea culminates in a two-part summit across episodes 8 and 9. That’s right: We finally meet survivors from other parts of the world.

The summit is initially intended to address the crisis consuming Ellora. Not only are Bender birth rates on the decline, but the fear-based Affliction is spreading thanks to the red Anomaly crystals growing beneath the city. The Bending Brigade can barely maintain order. But the visiting delegations reveal that some of Ellora’s problems are common. Benders are becoming scarce throughout the world, other Havens are struggling to produce enough food, and everyone seems to need resources their neighbors possess.

articles.title: 5 'Solo Leveling' Characters Who Deserved So Much Better
articles.summary: Jin-woo starts out as a weak E-Rank hunter trapped in a seemingly endless struggle to survive. Before long, though, he becomes an unstoppable force. His progression feels steady and earned, and his efforts to uncover the source of his abilities take him through a series of unforgettable fights.
body: Solo Leveling is the ultimate power fantasy. Based on Chugong’s web novel, which was later adapted into an acclaimed webtoon, the story takes place in a world where hunters wield supernatural abilities to battle dangerous beasts and protect humanity from extinction. Hunters are ranked by strength, but a video game-like interface known as the System lets our protagonist, Sung Jin-woo, climb the ranks and grow stronger at an astonishing pace.

It’s easy to see why Solo Leveling has become so popular. The series is an ever-escalating power fantasy that stays flashy and fun, even when it puts spectacle ahead of depth. That doesn’t make the story any less enjoyable. When its protagonist is relatable and easy to root for, straightforward world-building and likable supporting characters can be more than enough — especially in an anime elevated by impressive animation.

Before long, though, he becomes an unstoppable force.

articles.title: The Battlestar Galactica Board Game Is Making a Surprise Comeback Next Year
articles.summary: When it comes to board games, a frequent “Holy Grail” game (a term used to describe a game that someone has been hunting for, usually out of print and expensive) on many lists is Fantasy Flight Games’ Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game.
body: Details on this new edition are scant right now; all we have is that it’s a “new edition” that will feature “an updated design,” whatever that means, but I think the game is in safe hands. Overseeing this project will be Christian T. Peterson, the CEO of Ghost Galaxy and formerly the founder and CEO of Fantasy Flight Games and the creator of a little game called Twilight Imperium.

Recently, Fantasy Flight Games launched a similar campaign as the debut of its “Vault Series” with Arkham Horror Remastered (check out our interview and exclusive art reveal ), which seeks to accomplish a similar goal with the much-loved Arkham Horror Second Edition. Whether this will be a part of the Vault Series or not, seeing as it is being officially published by another group, remains to be seen, but awesome to hear nonetheless.
The campaign page for the new edition of Battlestar Galactica will be launching soon, so you and your wallet can rejoice.

articles.title: 27 Years Later, Linus' Final 'Peanuts' Quote Is a Brilliant Comic Strip Callback
articles.summary: Charles Schulz's Peanuts, for whatever reason, has one of the more dedicated fan communities on the internet. The Peanuts Fandom wiki is an invaluable resource for anything you might want to know about the strip, from obscure characters to running jokes to the gang’s unofficial cameo appearances in…
body: Somewhat more depressingly, the wiki features a rundown of the daily Peanuts strip that includes all of its various unofficial finales. As you flip through the last couple of months' worth of published Peanuts strips, you encounter footnotes about everything in the strip that’s now over.

By the end of January 2000, almost every character, interaction, catchphrase, and recurring scenario in Peanuts has appeared for the last time: the football gag (Oct. 24, 1999), the Great Pumpkin (Halloween 1999), Snoopy's weird cousin Spike (Dec. 21, 1999), Lucy Van Pelt (Dec. 13, 1999), etc. In most of those cases, Schulz hadn't been aware he was drawing a sendoff. He'd just been going about his usual business until he was suddenly forced into medical retirement.

As a result, Peanuts has no official final chapter besides Schulz's farewell note on Feb. 13, 2000. There are a couple of strips that feel like they've got some degree of subtext regarding Schulz's failing health, like Nov. 1, 1999 ("You're the last one... did you turn out the light?”) or Peppermint Patty's last appearance, but that's primarily an exercise left for the reader.

articles.title: Anya Taylor-Joy’s breakout movie gave horror a different kind of female lead
articles.summary: Anya Taylor-Joy has established herself as one of her era's most versatile actors. At 30, she's built a career across film and television, appearing in franchises like Super Mario and Mad Max, along with winning a Golden Globe for her role in The Queen’s Gambit.
body: The Witch follows a devout, isolated Puritan family in 1630s New England, a time when witches, myth, and folklore quietly stood at the root of most people’s everyday fears. Following their exile from the religious community due to a dispute with the church, a family of seven is forced to relocate to the outskirts of society, with the dark, unmapped woods mere feet away.

The film is steeped in its historical setting, and its characters speak a dense form of archaic English, with religion at the very center of their lives. That can be a tough watch for modern viewers, but The Witch ultimately tells a simple story about a family hitting its breaking point.

With no animals left to hunt and their crops rotting, William (Ralph Ineson) and his wife Katherine (Kate Dickie) are desperate. They spend their days bitterly arguing in their cramped home and blaming each other for everything that goes wrong. Their younger kids absorb the tension (and perhaps Black Phillip's devilish whispers), acting out in ways that make everyone's lives more difficult. Things boil over when the family’s newborn, Samuel, disappears under the watch of their eldest daughter, Thomasin (Anya Taylor-Joy).
points: Anya Taylor-Joy has established herself as one of her era's most versatile actors.
At 30, she's built a career across film and television, appearing in franchises like Super Mario and Mad Max, along with winning a Golden Globe for her role in The Queen’s Gambit.

articles.title: Clayface Ending Explained
articles.summary: The new movie Clayface marks the live-action film debut of the classic Batman villain but fans are obviously wondering if the film also introduces the DCU’s incarnation of the Caped Crusader.
body: Let's make this simple: You want to know if there are any mid- or post-credits scenes in Clayface. The answer is no.
We’re gonna dive into how Clayface ends, how the character’s design was created for the film, and yes, the Batman of it all… so read on!

While Batman is never even mentioned here, the movie does feature a scene set at the Wayne Community Centre. But let’s be clear: Batman already exists in Clayface’s Gotham City and in the DCU at large.

Of that version of the Caped Crusader, Gunn already confirmed last year that “this is the DCU Batman,” but the character was kept in silhouette because he was not yet ready to commit to a final costume design. Gunn said the animated cameo was “just a way to introduce that Batman is a part of this universe, he's an important part of this universe, and he has an impact on it.”

articles.title: After The BioWare Shutdown, Mass Effect Spiritual Successor Exodus Gets A New Look
articles.summary: In the wake of the news that EA has closed down BioWare and ended development on Mass Effect 5, Archetype Entertainment—co-founded by former BioWare devs Chad Robertson, James Ohlen, and Drew Karpyshyn—has given players a brand-new look at its upcoming title, a very Mass-Effecty sci-fi RPG called…
body: Specifically, Archetype has revealed a visual rework of its male player-character model. When GameSpot previewed Exodus in late August, the male version of protagonist Jun Aslan could be seen sporting a five-o'-clock shadow and very different bone structure. Now, he has a whole new face. In a new video uploaded to Archetype's YouTube channel today, Archetype general manager Chad Robertson showed off male-Jun's new look, which he explained is a result of player feedback.

"We've seen your conversations and feedback over the last few months around our male Jun character model," Robertson said. "We've been listening, and we take that feedback seriously. We've continued to refine Jun as we've worked on him and the rest of the game."
Archetype hasn't yet revealed Jun's female character model, but the devs say her reveal is on the way.

"Is FemJun on your mind?" a new post on the official Exodus website asks. "Ours too! And we’re happy to say yes, she’s coming... soon™. We’ve got something special cooking for her reveal, and we think it’ll be worth the wait."

articles.title: GTA 6’s New TV Trailer Is A Bit Different, See It For Yourself
articles.summary: GTA 6 's marketing push is ramping up substantially, and that includes with TV commercials. Eagled-eyes fans have discovered that the new GTA 6 TV spots actually contain some extended sequences, but just barely.
body: For starters, a 30-second TV spot cuts out the steamy shower scenes with Jason and Lucia from the launch trailer. While the shower scenes are gone in this edit, the new TV spot has a slightly longer shots of an airplane sequence and another with Jason and Lucia standing next to their car.

Jason playfully nudges Lucia, and in the TV spot, she nearly topples to the ground. The Xbox logo was also removed, presumably due to Rockstar's reported promotional deal with Sony. You can check out the comparison below ( via IGN ).

A 90-second version, meanwhile, includes the shower scenes, along with the slightly longer sequences seen in the 30-second version. If you saw these TV spots recently, you might not have even noticed any of these changes, but GTA 6 fan accounts are extremely dedicated and never miss anything.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and, yes, Xbox Series X|S, even though the TV ads for the game don't tell you that. Rockstar's marketing push for the game also includes real-life Burger Shot and Cluckin' Bell restaurants where you can buy GTA-branded food.

articles.title: A new Fallout 4 mod adds an entire town, but more importantly, it lets you join a gang
articles.summary: There's nothing I like more in a Fallout game then stumbling across some weird little settlement filled with oddball characters. So when I saw that this mod for Fallout 4 added a whole new town called Detour that's built on top of an overpass near Bedford Station, that was an instant download.
body: Better yet, the mod features new quests and over a dozen new characters voiced by real people—no AI was used!

But there's something better than that, even. I was delighted to discover that the town of Detour has its own gang. It's a small gang, sure: the overpass Detour is built on isn't particularly big and the town itself is pretty tiny, so there's not a whole lot of room for different factions to spring up. But that doesn't stop the members of the Detour Degens from occupying one little corner of the town where they hang out in matching jackets, smoking cigs, chugging from beer bottles, and looking tough.
Sort of. Look, the Detour Degens are no Tunnel Snakes, that's for sure. But they live on an overpass. They're doing their best.

There are a few different types of missions you can do to raise your reputation with the town of Detour, and besides helping out the sheriff with bounties and recovering stolen goods for a few of the merchants, you can also get in good with the gang. The two members of the Degens I met told me that the third member, their leader, was locked up and they wanted me to spring him.

articles.title: I’m Getting Very Worried About Skate Following EA Layoffs
articles.summary: Publisher Electronic Arts recently slashed 400 roles across its company, which resulted in the shuttering of legendary RPG studio BioWare. But also impacted by the layoffs was Skate developer Full Circle, and now I'm growing increasingly worried about the future of a franchise I waited so long to…
body: Part of EA's latest round of layoffs on October 21 included cutting an unspecified number of staffers to create a "very clear roadmap" that leads to a "healthier and more sustainable business." Then, as VGC noted on the same day, "many" of the developers at Full Circle are gone. This includes artists Brendan Vermeltfoort and Will Granda, seasonal creative director John Epler, and senior designers Adam Martinazzi and David Milne--all of whom posted the unfortunate news on LinkedIn.

It's always a bummer when talented developers lose their jobs at the hands of corporate greed, but this one stings for me personally. As a big Skate girlie, I was so stoked for the franchise to make a comeback, and even more stoked to get my hands on the game in September 2025.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Is Keeping Its Secrets Close To The Chest
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever players may have searched its beta with a fine-toothed comb, but Blizzard said there are still plenty of secrets waiting to be found come launch and beyond.
body: In a new WoW: Forever Podcast dedicated to the end of the beta, Blizzard made clear it's keeping many of the game's surprises close to its chest. Senior game designer Josh Greenfield said Blizzard had disabled some items and secrets for the beta. He gave an example of a new torch item that was originally turned off for the beta's first week, but later enabled to test out Forever's new lighting and fog tech. He said players can expect more of those types of surprises.

"There's definitely some secrets and stuff that we had turned off," Greenfield said when asked about still to be discovered secrets in the level 1-30 zones. "There's going to be things to discover that we didn't surface, suffice to say that."

Forever's beta had a maximum level of 30, meaning there is still a huge chunk of the game, including new zones, quests, dungeons, and raids, players haven't fully explored yet. When asked about items like a newly discovered sword in the beta that could potentially enable new playstyles, like a melee-focused "Battle Mage", Greenfield opted not to elaborate further.
points: World of Warcraft: Forever players may have searched its beta with a fine-toothed comb, but Blizzard said there are still plenty of secrets waiting to be found come launch and beyond.

articles.title: Smash Bros. director Masahiro Sakurai thinks gen-AI will cause a surge of unoriginal games, but says human creativity can't be replicated
articles.summary: Masahiro Sakurai has spoken about the pitfalls of generative AI use in game development, saying that while he believes the technology will result in a surge of unoriginal video games, human creativity - such as that shown by designers like Ico's Fumito Ueda - can't be replicated.
body: In an interview with Japanese news outlet Denfaminicogamer, Sakurai was asked about his time judging for the Game Designers Awards (a role he recently retired from) and his thoughts on the massive increase of game releases since the awards began. In 2010, 275 games were published on Steam, whereas more than 19,000 released this year.

"19,000 is amazing, but I think that number will increase even more from now on," Sakurai said (as translated from Japanese using Google Translate). "I'm sure of it. That's because AI will increase the number. However, I think most of them will become 'unprofitable titles'. There are too many to keep track of, and it's impossible to understand them all.

"When it comes to things created with AI... or things mass-produced with poor quality, I think most of them will simply be reproductions of systems seen in various other games. I think there are already a lot of those now."
points: Masahiro Sakurai has spoken about the pitfalls of generative AI use in game development, saying that while he believes the technology will result in a surge of unoriginal video games, human…

articles.title: Epic announces game jam where you have to use AI, then walks back the requirement
articles.summary: Unreal Engine maker Epic Games is running a game jam in November with thousands of dollars in prizes up for grabs. Contrary to so many art contests which ban the use of AI, participants in Epic's event are highly encouraged to use AI.
body: The theme of the 2026 Epic AI MegaJam will be revealed on November 11, and participating individuals and teams will then have from November 12–15 to produce their games with the help of AI tools.

Some will work in-person at a San Francisco event space, and there will be daily livestreams with progress updates. The winners in three categories will each receive $7,500, with smaller cash prizes for second and third place winners, as well as additional categories like "best team." Also on the table are "Development Continuation Grants of up to $50,000 per team."

Epic extended the invitation with a reference to The Matrix's 'red pill' scene, presenting red-pilled AI-driven development as an opportunity to "ship awesome games in a weekend," while old-fashioned blue-pilled development would have you "wait months to prototype." The hand offering the red pill features an extra finger, a reference to the common mistake made by AI image generators.
points: Unreal Engine maker Epic Games is running a game jam in November with thousands of dollars in prizes up for grabs.

videos.summary: Seen the anime? Play the update — if you’re ready…
body: Dive back into Night City with the free Edgerunners 2 Update for Cyberpunk 2077, featuring content inspired by Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. Take on a new quest that takes place before the anime’s raw, brutal story begins; carry on Jackie’s legacy with the Dual Wielding playstyle; and discover much more as you pick up the pieces in the City of (Broken) Dreams.
The Edgerunners 2 Update is out now on PlayStation 5.
#ps5 #ps5games #cyberpunk2077

videos.title: Final Fantasy Resonance - Launch Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE is the first FINAL FANTASY in HD‑2D! Available now PlayStation 5.
body: Return to the pixel‑art world of FINAL FANTASY, evolved from its classic roots. Travel with companions bound by fate and call on Visions, echoes of beloved FINAL FANTASY characters, to aid you in battle to uncover the truth behind a force that threatens to bring everything to ruin.

Begin your journey in FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE in the free demo and experience the story from the opening through the end of Chapter 1. Continue your adventure by carrying over your demo saved data to the full game.
